title: BALLAST: Bayesian Active Learning with Look-ahead Amendment for Sea-drifter Trajectories under Spatio-Temporal Vector Fields
anchored_claims: Proposition 1 shows that standard active-learning utility construction, which ignores the future trajectories of Lagrangian drifters, yields suboptimal observer placement decisions (Section 3.1, Proposition 1).

BALLAST's acquisition function uses an SPDE-based extended Gaussian process state f=[f, partial_t f]^T with Matern-3/2 temporal kernels to enable posterior sampling without the O(J*N_space^3*N_sampT^3) cost of naive sampling (Section 4.1, Section 4.2).

On synthetic Helmholtz ground-truth vector fields across 100 runs over 10 fields, BALLAST-aided sequential observer placement saves approximately 3 drifters (about 16% cost reduction) compared to uniform, Sobol, and expected-information-gain placement policies (Section 5.2).
On the high-fidelity SUNTANS ocean model over 100 independent runs, BALLAST achieves approximately 22% deployment cost savings relative to baseline placement policies (Section 5.3).

An ablation on the number of Monte Carlo vector-field samples J shows that J=20 achieves less than 1% utility gap regardless of decision time, balancing accuracy against computational cost (Section 5.1, Figure 4).
